q-85892.name: Question 1
q-85892.problem:
Given that the columns of $A$ are linearly independent, find the least-squares solution of $Ax=b$, where 

$\,$ $A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,b=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$
q-85892.worked_solution:
First of all, we write the given system in the form $Ax=b:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{A}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}]}}\overset{x}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{b}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}}\end{aligned}
$$

We can find the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{x}$ of the equation above by solving the corresponding normal equation, which we obtain by left-multiplying our original equation by ${A}^{T}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A\overset{^}{x} & ={A}^{T}b\end{aligned}
$$

Since the columns of $A$ are linearly independent, the matrix ${A}^{T}\,A$ is invertible. Therefore, multiplying by $({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}$ on the left, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{^}{x} & =({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}{A}^{T}b \\  & ={([\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}])}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & ={[\begin{aligned}6 & -3 \\ -3 & 2\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}6 \\ -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{3}[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ 3 & 6\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}6 \\ -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

[10−112−1]⏞A[x1x2]⏞x=[2−21]⏞b

q-40891.name: Question 2
q-40891.problem:
Given that the columns of $A$ are linearly independent, find the least-squares solution of $Ax=b$, where 

$\,$ $A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 4 \\ 2 & -2 & -2 \\ 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 2 & -2\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,b=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$
q-40891.worked_solution:
First of all, we write the given system in the form $Ax=b:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{A}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 4 \\ 2 & -2 & -2 \\ 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 2 & -2\end{aligned}]}}\overset{x}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{b}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}}\end{aligned}
$$

We can find the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{x}$ of the equation above by solving the corresponding normal equation, which we obtain by left-multiplying our original equation by ${A}^{T}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A\overset{^}{x} & ={A}^{T}b\end{aligned}
$$

Since the columns of $A$ are linearly independent, the matrix ${A}^{T}\,A$ is invertible. Therefore, multiplying by $({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}$ on the left, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{^}{x} & =({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}{A}^{T}b \\  & ={([\begin{aligned}2 & 2 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & -2 & 0 & 2 \\ 4 & -2 & 0 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 4 \\ 2 & -2 & -2 \\ 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 2 & -2\end{aligned}])}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & -2 & 0 & 2 \\ 4 & -2 & 0 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & ={[\begin{aligned}16 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 8 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 24\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}8 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{48}[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 6 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}8 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2} \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

q-85275.name: Question 3
q-85275.problem:
Find the least-squares solution to the system of linear equations given below. You're given that the columns of the corresponding coefficient matrix are linearly independent.

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}=6 \\ 2{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+2{x}_{3}=12 \\ -2{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=0 \\ 2{x}_{1}-2{x}_{3}=12\end{aligned}
$$
q-85275.worked_solution:
First of all, we write the given system in the form $Ax=b:$

$$
\overset{A}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & -2 & 1 \\ 2 & 0 & -2\end{aligned}]}}\overset{x}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]}}=\overset{b}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 12 \\ 0 \\ 12\end{aligned}]}}
$$

We can find the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{x}$ of the equation above by solving the corresponding normal equation, which we obtain by left-multiplying our original equation by ${A}^{T}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A\overset{^}{x} & ={A}^{T}b\end{aligned}
$$

Since the columns of $A$ are linearly independent, the matrix ${A}^{T}\,A$ is invertible. Therefore, multiplying by $({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}$ on the left, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{^}{x} & =({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}{A}^{T}b \\  & ={([\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 0 & 2 \\ -2 & 1 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & -2 & 1 \\ 2 & 0 & -2\end{aligned}])}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 0 & 2 \\ -2 & 1 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}6 \\ 12 \\ 0 \\ 12\end{aligned}] \\  & ={[\begin{aligned}9 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 9 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 9\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}54 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{9}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}54 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

$$

q-85905.worked_solution:
First of all, we write the given system in the form $Ax=b:$

$$
\overset{A}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 & 0 \\ 4 & 2 & 4 \\ 0 & -4 & 2 \\ 4 & 0 & -4\end{aligned}]}}\overset{x}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]}}=\overset{b}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}8 \\ 2 \\ 2 \\ -6\end{aligned}]}}
$$

We can find the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{x}$ of the equation above by solving the corresponding normal equation, which we obtain by left-multiplying our original equation by ${A}^{T}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A\overset{^}{x} & ={A}^{T}b\end{aligned}
$$

Since the columns of $A$ are linearly independent, the matrix ${A}^{T}\,A$ is invertible. Therefore, multiplying by $({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}$ on the left, we obtain

$$

q-85280.name: Question 5
q-85280.problem:
Consider the system $Ax=b$, where the matrix $A$ and the vector $b$ are given below. Given that the columns of $A$ are linearly independent, find the minimum value of $‖Ax-b‖.$

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 \\ -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}10 \\ 20 \\ -1 \\ 17\end{aligned}]
$$
q-85280.worked_solution:
First of all, we write the given system in the form $Ax=b:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{A}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 \\ -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}]}}\overset{x}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{b}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}10 \\ 20 \\ -1 \\ 17\end{aligned}]}} \\ Ax & =b\end{aligned}
$$

We can find the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{x}$ of the equation above by solving the corresponding normal equation, which we obtain by left-multiplying our original equation by ${A}^{T}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A\overset{^}{x} & ={A}^{T}b\end{aligned}
$$

Since the columns of $A$ are linearly independent, the matrix ${A}^{T}\,A$ is invertible. Therefore, multiplying by $({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}$ on the left, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{^}{x} & =({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}{A}^{T}b \\  & ={([\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & -2 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 \\ -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}])}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & -2 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}10 \\ 20 \\ -1 \\ 17\end{aligned}] \\  & ={[\begin{aligned}8 & -2 \\ -2 & 6\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}22 \\ 44\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{22}[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ 1 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}22 \\ 44\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 9\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The minimum value of $‖Ax-b‖$ is attained when $x=\overset{^}{x},$ which is the least-squares solution of the system $Ax=b.$ In this case, $A\overset{^}{x}$ represents the orthogonal projection of $b$ onto the column space of $A,$ and $‖A\overset{^}{x}-b‖$ is the distance between the vector $b$ and the column space. Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}A\overset{^}{x}-b & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 \\ -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}5 \\ 9\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}10 \\ 20 \\ -1 \\ 17\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-9 \\ -11 \\ -9 \\ 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, 

$$
‖A\overset{^}{x}-b‖=\sqrt{(-9)^{2}+(-11)^{2}+(-9)^{2}+{1}^{2}}=2\sqrt{71}.
$$

q-85284.problem:
Consider the system $Ax=b$, where the matrix $A$ and the vector $b$ are shown below. Given that the columns of $A$ are linearly independent, find the minimum value of $‖Ax-b‖.$

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 14 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]
$$
q-85284.worked_solution:
First of all, we write the given system in the form $Ax=b:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{A}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}]}}\overset{x}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{b}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 14 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}} \\ Ax & =b\end{aligned}
$$

We can find the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{x}$ of the equation above by solving the corresponding normal equation, which we obtain by left-multiplying our original equation by ${A}^{T}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A\overset{^}{x} & ={A}^{T}b\end{aligned}
$$

Since the columns of $A$ are linearly independent, the matrix ${A}^{T}\,A$ is invertible. Therefore, multiplying by $({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}$ on the left, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{^}{x} & =({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}{A}^{T}b \\  & ={([\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 1 & -1 \\ 1 & -1 & 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}])}^{-1}\,\,[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 1 & -1 \\ 1 & -1 & 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 14 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & ={[\begin{aligned}4 & 1 \\ 1 & 4\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}15 \\ 15\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{15}[\begin{aligned}4 & -1 \\ -1 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}15 \\ 15\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The minimum value of $‖Ax-b‖$ is attained when $x=\overset{^}{x},$ which is the least-squares solution of the system $Ax=b.$ In this case, $A\overset{^}{x}$ represents the orthogonal projection of $b$ onto the column space of $A,$ and $‖A\overset{^}{x}-b‖$ is the distance between the vector $b$ and the column space. Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}A\overset{^}{x}-b & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 \\ 3\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 14 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -4 \\ -8 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, 

$$
‖A\overset{^}{x}-b‖=\sqrt{{5}^{2}+(-4)^{2}+(-8)^{2}+{2}^{2}+(-1)^{2}}=\sqrt{110}.
$$
